questions.Q1: do pretrained heads beat randomly initialised heads after the same adapter training?
questions.Q2: does the typed-decisions head beat the coding head?
questions.Q3: does removing the coding context reduce the reference head's accuracy?

heads (all frozen; 31 tensors each: 24 c.coding: models/coding-decision-agent (REFERENCE, the head of every earlier result)
heads (all frozen; 31 tensors each: 24 c.random_1001 / _1002 / _1003: the same DecisionHead architecture built under torch seed 1001 / 1002 / 1003: PyTorch's default initialisation of every layer (the family a fresh head of this architecture starts from); per-tensor norms of every head are reported next to the result

not loaded from any checkpoint (reconcil: act_head.0/2 weight and bias (LAYA's abstain/escalate gate; our head's own gate is frozen and unused) and the scalar `temperature`

adapter training (identical for every he.init: DecisionHead built under torch seed = run seed, so every head gets the SAME initial adapter for a given seed
adapter training (identical for every he.schedule: cosine over all steps to 0.1 x, as the frozen trainer's adapter group
adapter training (identical for every he.checkpoint: lowest recorded-action loss on the development fold, every 25 steps

reproduction gate (stop interpreting if: coding head, seed 0, out of fold must be within 4 points of 77.89% (tools/laya_joint_v1.py adapter_only, same 303 pools and folds); the 3-seed cleaned VAL mean within 4.4 points of 76.09%
primary evaluation: 5-fold cross-validation on the 303 cleaned TRAIN pools (test fold k, development fold (k+1) mod 5, three folds fitted; trajectory-disjoint); per pool the mean over 3 seeds (seeds are NOT independent examples); paired differences with 2,000 bootstrap resamples of whole trajectories
primary comparisons (family of 6; two-si: coding: real context minus no context (same pools)
decision rule (development screening): a difference counts only if it is at least 5 points AND its corrected interval excludes 0. random_mean = per pool, the mean of the three random heads; the spread of the three is reported
no-context: every trained model is also scored with the no-context features on the 112 TRAIN pools that have them (test-time removal)
VAL: after the configuration is fixed: each head, adapter trained on folds 1-4, development fold 0, 3 seeds, scored ONCE on the 46 cleaned VAL pools with and without context. Development-exposed: a check, not confirmation; nothing is chosen on it
zero-training swap (diagnostic): the three Fable-trained adapters of laya-baseline-v1 (trained for the coding head) loaded unchanged in front of every head; scored on cleaned VAL and the 600 native items only (those adapters saw every TRAIN pool). A failure shows incompatibility of that adapter with that head; it does not by itself show why
native 600: reported for every model, information only (the items are the coding head's own decision types)

readings fixed beforehand.random within 5 points of coding: no demonstrated advantage of these pretrained heads under this adapter and recipe; it does NOT show that a better-trained general head could never help
readings fixed beforehand.typed beats coding by the rule: general-decision specialisation transfers to this Fable task; a reason to revisit general-decision training
readings fixed beforehand.probe beats coding: the pretrained-head system adds nothing over a linear read-out on these features (expected from earlier results)
readings fixed beforehand.any result: agreement with Fable only; not coding-task success; one backbone

leakage safeguards: folds trajectory-disjoint (asserted); VAL trajectories disjoint from TRAIN (asserted); no CAL / TEST in either dataset; each head's 31 tensors asserted identical before and after training; the zero-training adapters are never scored on TRAIN pools
